facts.fact_text: On 5 December 2011 the applicants took part in a public demonstration (a meeting) at Chistyye Prudy, Moscow.
The public demonstration on 5 December 2011 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged State Duma elections.
The demonstration on 5 December 2011 had been duly authorised by the mayor of Moscow.
The meeting on 5 December 2011 was conducted by the second applicant.
During the meeting on 5 December 2011, the first applicant addressed the participants with a speech calling for fresh, fair elections.
During the meeting on 5 December 2011, the first applicant described United Russia, the election frontrunner, as "a party of crooks and thieves".
After the demonstration on 5 December 2011, the applicants were arrested.
Both applicants were arrested at about 8.45 p.m. on 5 December 2011.
The applicants were charged with an administrative offence for refusing to comply with a lawful order of the police, in breach of Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The second applicant was convicted under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced to fifteen days' administrative detention.
The first applicant was convicted under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced to fifteen days' administrative detention.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, at the material time, provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of their official duties related to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the performance by them of their official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between 500 and 1,000 Russian roubles or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

The Federal Law on Assemblies, Meetings, Demonstrations, Marches and Picketing (no. 54-FZ of 18 August 2004) provided, at the material time, that a public event could be stopped if there was a real threat to life or the physical integrity of persons or property.

The Federal Law on Assemblies, Meetings, Demonstrations, Marches and Picketing (no. 54-FZ of 18 August 2004) provided, at the material time, that a public event could be stopped if the participants had acted unlawfully or the event organiser had knowingly breached the requirements of the Act as regards the conduct of the event (section 16).
According to the Government, the group of about sixty people walked along the road, obstructing the traffic and chanting slogans such as "This is our city!" and "Down with the police state!".
According to the Government, the marchers ignored the repeated demands of the police to stop and thereby prevented the police from carrying out their mission of securing public order.

The Tverskoy District Court of Moscow held that the first applicant obstructed the traffic and created a risk of accident while shouting out "Shame!", "This is our city!", "Russia without Putin!", "Down with the police state!".
The demonstration on 5 December 2011 had been duly authorised by the mayor of Moscow.
The applicants claimed that they were walking along the pavement, leaving the road clear for traffic.
According to the applicants, no one in the surrounded group put up any resistance.
Witness B. testified that the policemen had not given the second applicant any orders before arresting him.
Witness T. testified that he had not seen the first applicant resisting the arrest.
The first applicant requested that two video recordings of his arrest, shot by witnesses T. and A., be admitted as evidence in the administrative proceedings.

The requests to admit the video recordings were dismissed on the grounds that the court had no technical means of playing the recordings and that it would be unacceptable to use the devices provided by the defence.

The second applicant testified as a witness in the appeal hearing that both the first applicant and the second applicant were arrested virtually simultaneously, that the police officers did not give any orders, there was no disobedience on the part of the applicants, and that police officers I. and F. did not take part in their arrest and their court testimonies were false.
